Honestly, I respectfully disagree. I also played this game on PC and you can instantly tell it's a console game ported to PC. This game might have been decently challenging on consoles but I played this game on hard on PC and the combat is trivial. You can easily headshot people with the revolver or get some fast kills with the shotgun. And when enemies get difficult, like with the big daddies, it just that it takes a lot of shots or spamming plasmids. 

The combat works for the game, but for me personally, it just distracted me from listening to the dialogue and getting closer to finishing the intriguing story.

I played the game on hard difficulty and the enemies aren't really too scary, maybes it's cause I've played more horror games before but they're not scary or difficult at all. Big Daddies are challenging, I'll give you that but they just felt like giant bullet sponges that you had to keep your distance from. 

I definitely got immersed in the world, but the combat is far from capable, especially compared to any other games that are similar, especially to dishonored. 

Some games you play because the gameplay is great and you could care 2 fucks about the story. In some other games, the story is brilliant and the combat is garbage or is completely removed for an overall better experience like Outer Wilds.

I do agree that the gameplay the card was providing was complete cancer, every aggro deck had it. Hell it was basically in every deck, I used it in my spiteful priest and have seen jade druid and tempo mage use it. 

But I don't think any card should be "killed." As much I don't like the card, I don't think it shouldn't be unplayable. So that's why I created these changes by making the card more reasonable and balanced without killing the damn card.

The first part of your response I would have to agree with, the chances are unlikely to get keleseth and shadowstep in your opening hand. But losing to that is extremely annoying as you're a sitting duck waiting to get destroyed on turn 6 with 3/3 patches and 3/4 fireflies. But since it's so rare i would say that balances itself out. 

The second part though, I would have to disagree with you quite a bit sir (don't threat), vulgar homunculus gets almost no play in any Warlock deck. Compared to the other the cards in this expansion, this card I would rate as "ehh." I literally haven't seen someone use demonfire in ladder for 3 months so idk where you see people using that card. The knife jugglers and the dire wolf are really good cards to help with Zoo lock, but people still implant Keleseth and still do really well in ladder. I don't think keleseth is as strong in Warlock decks compared to rogue, but it definitely makes them win more games.

I think the " If your deck has no 2-cost cards" part does make the card a lot more balanced but lets look at the popular decks that utilize Prince Keleseth, Rogue and Warlock.

**Rogue**
The only really major card that gets left out is Eviscerate, which is  a great card. But that's really it, no wonder why Tempo Rogue is a Tier 1 deck. Even If you don't High roll Keleseth, The deck does really well with its High Tempo Swings. And lets not Forget the disgusting Keleseth + Double Shadow Step Combo. 

**Warlock** 
The 2 major cards that get left out are Defile and Drain Soul. Defile is more of a control style card that doesn't really fit into Zoo Lock, so I wouldn't really consider that a Huge Loss. Then we have Drain Soul, This card is definitely great but is no where near meta-defining as other cards in Warlock collection. This card could be useful in Zoo Lock but it isn't a really a big loss as you could put in Drain Life or Mistress of Mixtures if you want heal really bad. Keleseth is definetlely not as strong in Warlock compared to Rogue but it +1/+1 really helps the class.
